heading: Oceans, Seas and Water
description: Fifty illustrated topics exploring oceans, rivers, fresh-and-salty estuary boundaries, deep underwater waves, rain cycles, and ships.

entries.title: Every living thing created from water
entries.scientific_topic: Water and the origin and persistence of life
entries.scientific_finding: All known terrestrial life depends on water. Water is essential for cellular chemistry, metabolism and the biochemical processes of living organisms.
entries.connection: The verse states that every living thing was made from water. This has a broad connection with the fundamental role of water in known life.
entries.limitations: The verse is a theological statement, not a detailed account of how the very first living cells began or the chemical origin of life.
entries.research_status: Researchable; examine classical tafsir and the meaning of the Arabic expression.

entries.title: Water as a source of human life
entries.scientific_topic: Human reproduction and biological dependence on water
entries.scientific_finding: Human reproduction involves water-rich biological fluids, and human development depends on a fluid environment.

entries.title: Water returning to Earth after evaporation
entries.scientific_topic: Atmospheric water and the water cycle
entries.scientific_finding: Water continuously circulates between Earth's surface, oceans, land and atmosphere through evaporation, condensation and precipitation.
entries.connection: The verse describes the sky as possessing a returning or repeating quality, depending on translation and interpretation.
entries.limitations: The interpretation of the Arabic word in this verse is not limited to the modern water-cycle cycle. Do not claim that it explicitly describes the entire cycle.
entries.research_status: Interpretive; investigate classical Arabic usage and tafsir.

research_rules: Verify every Quran reference, Arabic word and translation before publication.
Read the full passage and surrounding verses, not just an isolated phrase.
Consult classical tafsir before assigning a modern scientific interpretation.
Distinguish the Quranic wording, classical interpretation and modern scientific explanation.
Do not claim that two seas never mix; water masses and estuaries do mix.
Do not claim that the Quran explicitly describes thermohaline circulation or internal waves.
Do not present deep-sea darkness as a technical scientific description without considering the parable in 24:40.
Do not claim that every form of rainwater is safe to drink.
Do not invent hadith, authenticity grades, scientific papers, authors or publication details.
Use peer-reviewed research and authoritative scientific institutions for specific scientific claims.
Treat the evidence grades as provisional and revise them when detailed research is completed.
A scientific similarity is not automatically evidence of a miraculous prediction.

NASA_WATER_LIFE.title: Why is water so important for life as we know it?
NASA_WATER_LIFE.supports: Water is essential for known life and cellular function; this does not explain abiogenesis.

USGS_WATER_CYCLE.title: Water cycle
USGS_WATER_CYCLE.supports: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff, infiltration, groundwater recharge and discharge.

USGS_GROUNDWATER.title: Groundwater Flow and the Water Cycle
USGS_GROUNDWATER.supports: Groundwater movement through pores and fractures and discharge to springs, streams and oceans.

USGS_GROUND_STORAGE.title: Groundwater Storage and the Water Cycle
USGS_GROUND_STORAGE.supports: Water stored in soil, pores, cracks and aquifers; much groundwater originates from infiltrating precipitation.

NOAA_ESTUARIES.title: Estuaries Tutorial: What is an estuary?
NOAA_ESTUARIES.supports: Estuaries are transition zones where freshwater and seawater meet; salinity varies with tides, weather and freshwater inflow.

NOAA_ESTUARY_MIXING.title: Estuaries Tutorial: Circulation
NOAA_ESTUARY_MIXING.supports: Fresh and salt water may stratify or mix; degree of mixing depends on estuary conditions.

EPA_WATER_TYPES.title: Water Body Types
EPA_WATER_TYPES.supports: Estuarine boundaries and salinity gradients are dynamic and change with tides, inflow, wind and seasons.

NOAA_DEEP_LIGHT.title: How far does light travel in the ocean?
NOAA_DEEP_LIGHT.supports: Light declines rapidly with depth; photosynthesis is generally not possible below the euphotic zone, and the deep aphotic zone receives no sunlight.

NOAA_WAVES.title: Why does the ocean have waves?
NOAA_WAVES.supports: Wind-generated surface waves, storm surge and tsunamis have distinct mechanisms; waves transfer energy.

NOAA_WIND_WAVES.title: Waves
NOAA_WIND_WAVES.supports: Wind strength, duration and fetch affect wave size; swells can travel far from storms.

OPENSTAX_BUOYANCY.title: Archimedes’ Principle and Buoyancy
OPENSTAX_BUOYANCY.supports: Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid; ship flotation depends on average density and displacement.

NOAA_PEARLS.title: How do oysters produce pearls?
NOAA_PEARLS.supports: Pearls form as molluscs deposit layers of nacre-like material around an irritant or foreign body.

SMITHSONIAN_PEARLS.title: Pearls of Wisdom
SMITHSONIAN_PEARLS.supports: Pearl formation in pearl oysters and nacre deposition.

NOAA_CORAL.title: Coral reef ecosystems
NOAA_CORAL.supports: Corals are animals; reef ecosystems support diverse marine life and provide ecosystem services.

NOAA_CORAL_SPECIES.title: What species live in and around coral reefs?
NOAA_CORAL_SPECIES.supports: Coral reefs provide habitat for many marine species.

UNEP_CORAL.title: Coral reefs
UNEP_CORAL.supports: Coral reef biodiversity, food security and coastal protection.

NOAA_FOOD_FISHERIES.title: Coral reef ecosystems
NOAA_FOOD_FISHERIES.supports: Marine habitats support fisheries and food resources; ecological services depend on healthy ecosystems.

NOAA_WAVES_STORM.title: What causes ocean waves?
NOAA_WAVES_STORM.supports: Surface waves, storm surge and tsunamis; different physical causes and hazards.

critical_cautions: Water is essential to all known life, but this does not mean science has established how life first originated.
Freshwater and seawater meet and can mix. Estuaries often contain salinity gradients or stratification, but the interface is dynamic, not an impermeable wall.
Qur'an 24:40 must be read in its parable context; deep-ocean darkness is a scientific fact but should not be claimed as the verse's definite technical subject.
The phrase 'waves above waves' should not automatically be equated with internal waves; multiple wave phenomena exist and textual interpretation needs separate evidence.
Storm waves, storm surge and tsunamis are different phenomena and should not be conflated.
Rainwater is not automatically safe to drink; contamination can occur during atmospheric passage, collection, storage or handling.
Pearls are produced by certain molluscs through nacre deposition; avoid oversimplified claims that every pearl is formed around a grain of sand.
Corals are animals, and coral reefs are complex ecosystems; don't conflate coral with all marine 'treasures'.
Buoyancy is explained by fluid mechanics and displacement; the existence of ships is not by itself a scientific prediction.
Scientific descriptions of the hydrological cycle are modern explanatory models; individual Qur'anic verses should not be made to carry details absent from their wording.
